sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Brings in the needed helpers, the outcome colours and the shared types. The header explains that the file shows success and failure recipes, the heat map and case profiles.
sections.why: Shared helpers keep citation display and names consistent with other views.

sections.name: STANCE_CLASS, STANCE_GLYPH, STANCE_LABEL
sections.title: Stance colours, symbols and labels
sections.what: Gives each stance a background colour, a single symbol and a readable label. Strength is green, weakness is red, mixed is grey, and insufficient is pale.
sections.why: Lets the same judgement look the same in every table and list.
sections.watch_out: The symbol for insufficient evidence is short text, which may be hard to read on small screens.

sections.name: Panel, Kicker
sections.title: Panel and section heading
sections.what: Two small building blocks: a bordered white box with scrolling, and a small red heading above a section.
sections.why: Keeps the layout the same across the case views.

sections.name: Pill, hasCases
sections.title: Selectable pill and case check
sections.what: A rounded button that highlights when selected, and a check that confirms a run has at least one graded case before the case views are shown.
sections.why: The pills switch between pillars and pages. The check stops the case views from opening with no content.
sections.watch_out: The case check is the gate for these views. If it is changed, the views may open with empty data.

sections.name: RecipesView
sections.title: Recipes for success and failure
sections.what: Shows one pillar at a time with its headline, what separated the best from the worst cases, failure modes from cautionary tales, and recipe practices from successful deliveries. Each item lists the projects it came from.
sections.why: Lets a reader see what to copy and what to avoid for each pillar.
sections.watch_out: If the selected pillar has no lessons, the view shows a message rather than an empty table, which can hide a problem in the analysis.

sections.name: HeatMapView
sections.title: Project by pillar heat map
sections.what: Shows a table with one row per graded project and one column per pillar. Each cell is coloured by its stance. Rows are grouped into successful deliveries and cautionary tales. Clicking a row or cell can open that project's profile.
sections.why: Gives a quick overview of where projects are strong or weak, and links to the detail.
sections.watch_out: A cell with no stance is shown as insufficient evidence, so a missing judgement looks like a weak result at a glance.

sections.name: PillarCitedList
sections.title: Cited statement list
sections.what: Lists statements tied to a pillar, with the pillar name and citation marks.
sections.why: Gives a plain list of cited points that can be read without the table.

sections.name: CaseTwoPager (part 1)
sections.title: Case profile, first page
sections.what: Shows a list of graded cases on the left, grouped by success and cautionary, with the featured ones marked. On the right it shows the selected case's headline, outcome, performance, and the snapshot page with outcome, context, pillar stances, what worked and what went wrong. The first case shown is the featured one, or the first in the list.
sections.why: Gives a one-page summary of each project, so the reader does not need to read the whole analysis.
sections.watch_out: Choosing the first case uses the featured case or the first list entry, so an empty case list shows the no-case message instead.

sections.name: CaseTwoPager (part 2)
sections.title: Case profile, second page
sections.what: Shows the second page of the case profile, with its timeline of dated milestones and the full list of graded facts with their pillar tags. Switching pages is done with the pills at the top.
sections.why: Lets readers check the evidence behind the snapshot.
sections.watch_out: The facts list uses the case's fact ids to find facts. Facts with missing ids are dropped silently.

sections.name: PillarCaseStances
sections.title: Strengths and weaknesses for one pillar
sections.what: For one pillar, lists each project that shows a strength and each that shows a weakness, with the group it belongs to and its citations. If none exist, it says so.
sections.why: Lets readers compare how the cases did on one theme.
sections.watch_out: Each list uses only cases with a stance on this pillar, so a project without a stance does not appear in either list.

summary: This file draws the case-based views of a lessons run: recipes for success and failure per pillar, a heat map of projects by pillar, and two-page profiles for each case.
purpose: Lets users see which practices worked and which failed for each pillar, and compare the graded cases side by side with their sources.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The file header says every statement must carry its fact citations and that a stance without one shows as insufficient evidence instead of being guessed.
how: It defines colours, symbols and labels for each stance. Then it draws the pillar recipes, the heat map table, the list of cited pillar statements, the two-page case profile with a snapshot and a factbase page, and a per-pillar strengths and weaknesses list. Clicking a project in the heat map or the list can open its profile.
inputs: A run result that includes the framework pillars, projects, facts and the case analysis. Some views also take a project id to open first.
outputs: Screen panels, tables and lists that show stances, cited statements and profiles.
risks: Views depend on several lists being present. A missing list might show a message instead of content, which could hide a problem in the run. Stances without citations are shown as insufficient, so the views can look sparse for a weak run.
debug: If a case is missing, check that the case analysis was produced for the run and that the project id matches. If a stance looks wrong, check the citations on that stance. If a pillar is empty, check that the pillar id matches between the framework and the lessons list.
